about: An enumeration of the grammar, phonology and core lexis a Goethe-Zertifikat A1 (Start Deutsch 1) candidate is expected to hold, restated in our own words from the CECRL A1 descriptors and the structure the Goethe-Institut publishes for the level. A working restatement for measuring this corpus, not a reproduction of any awarding body's document.

communicative-functions.note: Some A1 functions appear among the points, but the complete official communicative construct is not yet enumerated.

grammar.note: This working restatement is measurable but is not source-closed against a complete published Goethe A1 grammar list.

phonology-orthography.note: The file contains sound and spelling points, but its source does not publish a complete finite dimension list.

lexicon.note: Core themes are represented, but the full official A1 word list has not yet been restated into probes.

probeSemantics: A point counts as COVERED when every atom in `probe` is introduced by some lesson in the track. `probe: null` means no atom in the corpus corresponds to this point, which is a finding rather than a gap in the data -- so a null probe counts as UNCOVERED and is reported by name.

points.label: three genders, not predictable from meaning
the five plural patterns (-e, -er, -n/-en, -s, zero)
points.note: Partly owned and deliberately not probed. Chapter 1 teaches that every plural takes die, chapter 22 teaches die Jahre, and the -e-with-umlaut break has its own atom. No lesson names the five patterns as a set, so a probe would claim more than the corpus teaches.

points.label: compound nouns take the gender of the last element
nominative and accusative forms
points.note: The chapter GE-C14-einen promised. All four atoms, because the point is the CONTRAST: den is the new article, the rule says only the der row moves, and einen and keinen are the two words the reader was already saying that move with it.

points.label: dative forms after common prepositions
points.note: The dative is named (GE-GRAMMAR-DATIVE-01, on mir) but only on pronouns. No article form and no preposition governs it yet.

points.label: personal pronouns in the accusative
points.note: sie and es are not listed because they are identical to their nominative forms -- probing them would resolve against the nominative atoms and claim a distinction the language does not make.

points.label: du / ihr / Sie as a register choice
possessives mein, dein, sein, ihr
points.note: GE-LEX-MEIN-01 is a NEW atom, not GE-LEX-MEIN-NAME-IST-02: mein was inside a fixed phrase and the phrase atom cannot demonstrate the word.

points.label: attributive adjective endings after the definite article
points.note: The two adjective-ending atoms the track owns (guten Tag, gute Nacht) are ACCUSATIVE endings after a frozen ein-phrase, not the definite-article paradigm this point asks for. Probing them would be a mis-claim.

points.label: separable verbs and where the prefix goes
modal verbs koennen, muessen, moechten
points.note: The bracket atom is listed with the three verbs because a modal without an infinitive at the end of the sentence is half the point.

points.label: the past participle in ge- ... -t / -en
points.note: Both families and the wrapper. The -t half was owned; the -en half was USED in gegangen and never named, which is why this point read as absent while the corpus was already saying it.

points.label: reflexive verbs with sich
points.note: The rule as well as the word: mich, dich, uns and euch already did this job and no lesson said so, so the construction was demonstrated in freut mich for forty-seven chapters and owned by nobody.

points.label: doch as the answer that contradicts a negative
W-questions: wer, was, wo, wann, wie, warum
points.note: All six, because the point names all six. Three were already taught and three are new; listing only the new ones would let the point read as closed if one of the old lessons were retired.

points.label: accusative: fuer, ohne, durch, gegen, um
points.note: Untaught as a class. um appears inside es ist ein Uhr and is not taught as a preposition.

points.label: dative: mit, nach, bei, seit, von, zu, aus
points.note: Untaught as a class, and blocked behind A1-ART-05: the dative article has to exist before a dative preposition can be shown governing one.

points.label: two-way prepositions in and auf
points.note: in and auf are both owned as words, from chapters 5 and 4. What is missing is the two-way rule that makes them choose a case.

points.label: time: am, im, um
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: time: heute, morgen, gestern, jetzt, immer, oft
points.note: Two of six owned: morgen (tomorrow, with its capital-splitting contrast against Morgen) and gestern. heute, jetzt, immer and oft have no atoms.

points.label: place: hier, dort, links, rechts
points.note: Untaught.

points.label: degree: sehr, ein bisschen, zu
points.note: One of three owned: sehr, from chapter 3.

points.label: gern with a verb to express liking
the verb bracket, with the second part at the end
points.note: The separable prefix demonstrated the bracket and never named it; GE-GRAMMAR-VERBKLAMMER-01 names it, and names the prefix, the participle and the cancelling nicht as three earlier instances of one habit.

points.label: coordination with und, oder, aber, denn
weil and the verb-final clause
points.note: The word and the movement, because weil without verb-final order is not weil.

points.label: ch after front and back vowels
final devoicing of b, d, g
the eszett and when ss is written instead
z as ts, and w as v
word stress on the stem
points.note: Shown repeatedly and never named. Four lessons say where the stress falls in one word (kaffee-stress is a registered sound tag); no lesson generalises it to the stem.

points.label: numbers 0-100
points.note: One to twenty owned outright, with the digit-plus-zehn rule and zwanzig's etymology. null, the -zig tens and the einundzwanzig order are untaught, so the top four fifths of the range cannot be said.

points.label: telling the time
points.note: Partly owned: es ist ... Uhr, Stunde, Mittag, Mitternacht, Zeit, frueh, spaet. halb, Viertel and the vor/nach split are untaught, so only whole hours can be told.

points.label: countries, nationalities, languages
points.note: One word owned: Deutsch, as the language in ich lerne Deutsch. No country, no nationality.
